Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tflplanner (development version)

  • An edit through the sheets keeps what only the spec holds (#415, 0.0.2.9235). When a screen that still edits the sheets (the ARD, the page, a listing, …) edits a report, its file takes from the sheets only the parts the edit changes – the label, the ARD, the data, the codelists, the page, a content item and its arguments – and keeps the rest as the spec has it, with the values the sheets cannot hold (a content argument written straight into the spec, a page key). A draft (the unsaved changes kept for a reload) also keeps the spec’s files the session changed, and taking it back gives them back; a draft made before files changed outside the app is merged by its sheets, as before.

  • A study with no report keeps its YAML spec (#413, 0.0.2.9234). A study saved before its first report has no spec/outputs/ folder; its spec/toc.yml now makes it a YAML spec all the same, so the planner’s spec holds a tfl_study_spec (it was a plain list, and the study reopened with no spec) and its programs are written from it.

  • The programs are written from the report files’ items (#411, 0.0.2.9233; step B2). A report program’s report part is tflspec’s tfl_report_code() and tfl_report_path() of the report as its file says it, a table’s plan tfl_content_code() of its content’s items, and programs/tfl/report_setup.R tfl_report_setup_code() of the study’s defaults: an argument the sheets cannot hold is in the program. The programs of the sample study are the same, byte for byte. The sheets still write a planner without a spec (a new study not yet saved, the company standards), one whose edits are not saved yet (the same code, without waiting for the whole study’s files), a listing’s data and columns, a figure’s design and a table normalized in its data part. The help of the variables’ order says the program’s plan_labels() and plan_levels(variable = ). tflspec >= 0.0.24.9147.

  • Docs: the Pages’ top bar is the package icon’s colour, red #7a2734 (#408, 0.0.2.9232), as rtfreporter’s bar is its icon’s navy.

  • The study’s model is its YAML spec (#407, 0.0.2.9231; step B1). A study’s planner holds the spec itself – the study’s files and one tfl_output a report – and the sheets the screens edit are a view of it (tflspec’s tfl_sheets_from_spec()). An edit of the sheets goes back to the files it changes only: a save after opening with no change writes no definition file, an edit of one report writes that report’s file, and a report the edits do not touch keeps its file as it is (what the sheets cannot hold included). tflspec >= 0.0.24.9139.

  • The table builder shows the content as the plan’s cards (#397, 0.0.2.9230). One card a function call – its fields that function’s arguments only – in the content’s order, under the plan bar with two separators: the table skeleton (which ARD values go to which rows, columns and cells) and finishing (labels, order, digits, pages). Each card is its meaning and its name (“Analysis variables (variable)”), the study default’s mark and Revert, real fields for the arguments (widths, rounding, the row filter through the condition builder, the level order by drag, comparisons, statistic groups, nesting, paging, row groups, hidden columns, cell styles) and R text for the rest; the whole program is in Code, a line jumping to its card. A card switched off stays (off: not in the code); its menu removes it; Add brings the others, placed by tflspec’s rank. Defaults the ARD tells are filled in with the mark “from the ARD”: a Total column when the ARD has overall rows, the factor order of the levels, the labels. A level order comes from the table’s own, else the report’s code list, else the ARD’s factor, else as first seen, the source said beside it. The rows are assigned as dragged, the analysis variables’ block removable (a table of one variable), the stack’s subgroup offered as rows (an Overall Response table), the row text chosen. tflspec >= 0.0.24.9137.

  • A table’s data is no longer saved per report (#405, 0.0.2.9229; the owner’s decision: the deliverable is the report). A table’s program no longer ends with saveRDS() to output/ard/<output_id>.rds; the report’s ARD is in the study ARD (output/ard/ard.rds) by output_id. The official run no longer lists the file among those it made (an earlier run’s compares as “not made” once), and study_status() loses its ard column (the file’s time, not shown on the status screen).

  • A table’s program normalizes its ARD in the table’s pipe (#402, 0.0.2.9228; tflspec >= 0.0.24.9137, its #302). With no process code and the company’s template left at the built-in one, the data part leaves ard (the report’s rows of the study ARD, saved to output/ard/<output_id>.rds) and the report part writes plan <- ard |> normalize_ard(hierarchy = ..., overall = ..., stack = ...) |> table_plan(...) |> plan_*(), the arguments from the report’s definitions as before; the separate data <- normalize_ard(...) line is gone. A table whose process code, company template or own data step makes data keeps plan <- table_plan(data, ...), and so does one whose content step is its own code. SAMPLE-01’s RTFs are the same.

  • The sample study SAMPLE-01 runs on tflspec’s oncology sample data (#400, 0.0.2.9227; the owner’s decision: the bundled onco data are the tfl series’ sample data). SAMPLE-01’s ADaM are tflspec’s simulated study XYZ-ONC-01 (Drug X vs Control; tflspec >= 0.0.24.9136): ADSL with its screen failures, ADAE, ADVS’s systolic blood pressure and ADTTE. The outputs are the same ones, each on the new study: the screen failures (T-14-1-4) are ARMNRS == "SCREEN FAILURE" (no arm), the screened subjects (T-14-1-5/6) have them as a column of their own (a derived ARMGRP) and the Asian sub-categories from the country, the disposition (T-14-1-2) is the end of study status (ongoing in follow-up, discontinued), the blood pressure (T-14-2-1/3, F-14-2-1) is at week 24 = cycle 9 day 1, and the time-to-event table and figures (T-14-2-2, F-14-2-2/3/4) are the time to the first treatment-emergent skin disorder (TTSKIN), Drug X against Control. pharmaverseadam is no longer used (its copyright holders leave DESCRIPTION; inst/COPYRIGHTS names tflspec’s data). The example TOC workbooks (inst/extdata/SAMPLE-01_TOC*.xlsx) are made again from it. The sample is written by tflspec 0.0.24.9136, whose tables keep their variables’ order as plan_levels(variable = ) (tflspec #300).

  • A double click on a filtered list opens the row double-clicked (#398, 0.0.2.9226; the user’s report). The report list filtered to Figure opened the third report of the whole list for the third figure: the lists are drawn on the server, so the browser’s row number is the row’s place among those shown; it is now read through the rows shown. The study list (its search over ten studies) the same.

  • A study’s definition is tflspec’s YAML spec (#395, 0.0.2.9225; the user’s decision of 2026-10-15). study.yml and spec/ – data.yml (the data catalog), defaults.yml (what every report has), toc.yml (the reports, their order and files), patterns/<name>.yml and one file a report, spec/outputs/<id>.yml (its ARD analyses, data, content and page) – are what the app reads and writes, through tflspec (tfl_sheets_from_yaml(), tfl_yaml_from_sheets()); the screens are as before. A save writes each file only when its text changed (one report changed: its file, and the TOC when its list changed). The workbooks (table_spec.xlsx, report_spec.xlsx, listing_figure_spec.xlsx, ard_definition.json, spec/figures/) are gone: a folder that still has them says to convert it (tflspec::tfl_convert_sheets_to_yaml()) or to import the workbooks. Outside edits (#274) are per file, compared with the study as its files say it, and only the parts that changed are taken in. Export writes the YAML files and one flat workbook to read or edit in Excel (tflspec’s tfl_write_spec_xlsx()); Import takes YAML files, a folder or zip of them, that workbook (when edited after the YAML beside it), or the workbooks of an earlier tflplanner (converted by tflspec). The sample study is made again as YAML: its programs are the same, its RTFs too but the time stamp (its ARD program in the TOC’s order). The programs’ header lines name the report’s file. export_spec(), import_spec(), read_planner() and write_planner() are gone from the API (the workbooks are no longer the study’s). Needs tflspec >= 0.0.24.9124.

  • The shift table returns with the unified builder (#378, 0.0.2.9224). Its template is hidden from the list for now (options(tflplanner.shift_template = TRUE) shows it): it is to choose its data among the study’s datasets, its parameters from the data, and to check BNRIND / ANRIND first.

  • A hierarchy table’s rows are the table’s (#375, 0.0.2.9224; the user’s principle: the ARD’s variables are defaults; the layout belongs to the content step). The builder’s “Rows” card mirrors “Columns”: the row variables, outermost first, among the ARD’s groups and hierarchy (by default its other groups, then the hierarchy; drag to reorder; a group of the ARD – a stratum – outermost), written to tables$rows / tables$label only, never to the ARD’s analysis; the outermost a page each (layout$group_page); “The any-event row” (tables$overall_label); and “Order”, one a row variable: by name, or the code list’s order when it has one (a factor sorts by its levels), or most frequent first with the tie in the choice (“ties by name” / “ties in the code list’s order”; a stratum is not ordered by its count), “Counted in” beside them. A stratum comes before the any-event row and has no summary row of its own. A hierarchy level left out is not written: the card says this ARD cannot make that table, with “Put it back” and a link to step 1’s analysis.

  • A shift table started from the data (#378, 0.0.2.9224; core gap #2 as corrected: tflspec’s LB example shows the engine does it). “Apply a template” has a third kind, Shift (baseline x worst after): the data (ADLB), the population (ADSL), the group, the parameters (a page each), the baseline and the post-baseline category (BNRIND / ANRIND, BTOXGR / ATOXGR), the records counted (ONTRTFL == "Y"), the worst order (best to worst; normal ranges NORMAL, LOW, HIGH) and a Total column. first_shift_table() writes each subject’s worst record of a parameter (an analysis data of R of its own), one categorical analysis by parameter, group and baseline – with a Total, over the records and the same again as the total, so no column is stated twice – the categories’ code lists, and a table with each group over its baselines, the parameter heading its page, at 8 points. The header prints no N: a group’s subjects differ from one parameter’s page to the next, and a header’s {n} is one number a column.

  • SOC / PT by worst severity or grade, from the data (#376, 0.0.2.9224; core gap #2 as corrected: the engine does it, the GUI did not). The hierarchy starter has an optional “By severity / grade (columns)” (AESEV, ATOXGR …): the grade joins the analysis’s by and the table’s columns, under each group with its N, and its levels are written in order as the report’s code list – cards counts each subject once, at the last level it has, so at its worst: of the SOC for the SOC row, of the PT for the PT row. Not with a Total column (it would drop the grade too). first_hierarchy_table(grade = ).

  • The table builder edits a hierarchy table (SOC / PT) (#375, 0.0.2.9224). It used to send such a table to the sheets (Details). It now opens with what such a table has: its columns (the variable, the arms’ order, Total), its column header, its statistics (n (%) and the decimals), and a Rows card of its own: the order of each term (the user’s request: rules are set per level) – by name (the code list’s order when the report has one for it) or most frequent first, ties by name – written as tables$sort. An order of the sheets’ own shows as such, with a link back to the card’s (SOC by name, PT most frequent first). An outer term most frequent first is its own row’s count (-n@group1), and “Counted in” says whose count: every column together, the Total column or one arm (-n[Total]; rtfreporter >= 0.8.2.9046, #624). The card also names the “any event” row (the table’s overall_label, #379; blank: no such row). The starter writes the same per-level order, and its “Any TEAE” in overall_label rather than a rework line of its own. A summary table’s rows are never written into it, and a hierarchy counted of a denominator has the subjects per group of its header. (The “Any TEAE” row’s name follows once tables$overall_label is on main.)

  • A hierarchical table started from the data (#374, 0.0.2.9224; the user’s decision after the template evaluation, dev-rep #5). A table’s “Start from the data” in Add a report is “Apply a template” now (the user’s choice; the figure designer’s word), a list of kinds: a summary table (demographics …) as before, or a hierarchical table (SOC / PT, ATC / drug … – its terms are chosen). The kind is chosen, never switched by the data. The hierarchy asks the data (ADAE), the population flag (of ADSL), the group, the terms (AEBODSYS | AEDECOD; CMCLAS | CMDECOD for medications), the records counted (TRTEMFL == "Y") and a Total column, and writes what a table made by hand has (first_hierarchy_table()): the analysis set and its subjects (adsl_saf), the records kept to them (adae_saf), one hierarchical analysis (over_variables = TRUE, percents of the set’s subjects), the table (most frequent first within each group), the SOC / PT column header and a page that does not split a group – the rows of the sample’s T-14-3-1. Before, choosing ADAE in “Start from the data” wrote a summary of its columns, and a first SOC / PT table took seven screens.

  • The study tab: Title, Short title, Study ID; no veil while a field is edited (#386, 0.0.2.9223; the user’s request). The “Protocol” box was a second copy of the Study ID, and “protocol” usually means the long title. The tab now has the Title, a Short title (new short_title in study.yml; {STUDY_SHORT_TITLE} in a header or footer; study_short_title in programs/study_setup.R; create_study(short_title = )) and the Study ID, read-only (it is the folder’s name and cannot be changed here; {STUDY_ID} in a header is it). A study whose STUDY_ID token says something else keeps that value, so its headers do not change; the tab says so and offers “Use the Study ID”. Editing a field (text, text area, select) or pressing Save no longer greys the page and shows the hourglass after 0.4 s (#51); the veil stays for opening a study and switching a tab or a report. More on the study tab: the Files section is three groups (Export, Import definition files, Restore from a backup), each a name and a “?” (the long text is the help); the sample study has keys (id, output, source: an ARD function of its own it does not use, programs/ard/functions/ard_cv_geomean.R) and a setup code with the libraries and commented options; and the study’s Title, Compound, Phase and Description are tokens too ({STUDY_TITLE}, {STUDY_COMPOUND}, {STUDY_PHASE}, {STUDY_DESCRIPTION}, with {STUDY_SHORT_TITLE}; named as study_setup.R’s variables), filled from study.yml for a header, footer, title or footnote that says one, and shown after each field’s label. The company standards’ setup code gains options(warn = 1) (a run’s log shows where a warning came from; nothing in the numbers changes), and the keys’ help says source is added when a function is made in Own ARD functions.

  • The Data tab: files and datasets on one screen (#388, 0.0.2.9222; the user’s request). The file list (All / SDTM / ADaM / Other, an “Into” folder) and the Datasets definition were two places. Now the Datasets grid has folder pills (ADaM | SDTM | Other) over it: the rows of the folder you are in (a row with no file by its level), the file’s size beside, and Add files puts files into the open folder. A file put in a folder gets a row when the Data tab is opened, on Refresh and on upload – now the other folder and subfolders too, and when a name has several files (adsl.rds, adsl.xpt) the row uses the one read first (rds, parquet, csv, xpt, sas7bdat); the note under the grid says the names with several files and the dataset names the catalog has twice. catalog_name_clashes() is new. Files and rows with no counterpart are said, nothing is dropped. The datasets sheet and the generated programs are unchanged (no migration). ARDs taken in stay on their own panel, with a note under the grid. The population is said where it is chosen (part 2 of #388): one short line at each place – an analysis’s Data, 1-1’s Population, the report’s population, the Populations tab and the denominator’s group (“Analysis sets (their subjects)”) – and an analysis data that is only a dataset kept to a set is the one line for it in an analysis’s Data list (its “dataset x population” twin is left out, unless the analysis reads it). Part 3: the Populations grid has a label column (tflspec 0.0.24.9111, ichirio/tflspec#252: the text a header prints, also the analysis set’s name in ARS): {OUTPUT_POPULATION} reads the sheet’s label first, then the company standards’ note, the flag’s label, the id, as before; a new study copies the company’s note into it. Blank: nothing changes. A workbook written with label does not read on an earlier tflspec, so DESCRIPTION asks for 0.0.24.9111 – merge tflspec#252 first, tflplanner right after. The sample study’s populations carry labels (Safety Analysis Set, Screen Failures, Enrolled Set); its reports are byte for byte as before.

  • tflspec 0.0.24.9112: tfl_fig_r() is tfl_r() (#390, 0.0.2.9221; the YAML spec’s one class for R code in a definition, every kind). A figure design’s R code is read, kept and written as before. (Pair of ichirio/tflspec#254: merge that first.)

  • Report sets and official runs are two things, named so (#387, 0.0.2.9220; the user’s request). What the app called a “batch” was two things: the choice of reports (a named set of them) and the run that makes the results. The set is now a report set (the Runs tab’s “Report set”, the report list’s “Report sets” column), the run an official run and its record a run folder (runs/<date>_<time>_<name>/). Report sets are made on the Runs tab only: filter the reports, tick the shown (or untick them), save the ticks under a name; the per-report “Batches…” box is gone (the button opens the Runs tab). What is stored is unchanged (the report list’s batches column, batch_sets(), run_batch()): no migration. The ids’ order: a new report goes to its numeric place, a TOC’s reports come in the TOC’s order, and “Sort by ID” (its hint says numbers as numbers) sorts the whole list. The report set’s box and its buttons stay in view when the run’s report list is folded; the inputs, selects and buttons of a row (the Runs tab’s set row and filter, the report list’s search) are one height.

  • An official run keeps going when the app closes; the launcher when its port is taken (#373, 0.0.2.9219; the user’s request). An official run (run_batch()) used to stop with the app’s R process – closing the browser, [Close], an update – and leave its ARD and reports half made. It now runs detached, recorded in the home (live_runs/); an app opened later shows it running (the Runs tab, the study list) and says how it went; a study runs one official run at a time, and [Close] says the run goes on. A preview still stops with the app. No update installs packages while an official run goes on (update_tflplanner(), the “update and launch” shortcut). When the shortcut finds its port taken: this version answering – it opens it; a tflplanner the launcher started that is another version or does not answer – it asks 「古いアプリが動いています。止めて起動し直しますか？」 (saying that an official run goes on), and stops it only on yes; a tflplanner in an R session of its own (RStudio) or another program – it leaves it and starts on the next free port. Each case is written to launcher.log. The app serves its version and process at /tflplanner-health/health.txt for this.

  • The tables sheet’s new column stat_groups (tflspec 0.0.24.9105, rtfreporter #619): one record’s statistics in two columns, N in one and the rate and its CI in the next, with no mutate() in the table’s code. Its help is translated.

  • An AE table’s “Subjects with at least one TEAE” row from the definition (tflspec #236, with tflspec 0.0.24.9104). A table without normalization of its own (and the company’s template the built-in data <- normalize_ard(ard)) now gets the line its definitions say, tflspec::tfl_normalize_code(): the hierarchy of its hierarchical analysis – each SOC row with its counts – and the any-event row of the tables sheet’s new overall_label. A table without either is as before; the sample’s AE table keeps its own line.

  • The CDISC ARS export opens a dialog (Study tab, Files): what the ARS holds (its analyses, outputs, analysis sets and data subsets), its checks and what it leaves out, one row each, before anything is written; a row’s report is a link that goes to it, as a Review item does. The profile is chosen there – CDISC (to exchange, the default) or siera (to run with siera), which the screen could not export before – and either JSON only or the zip of JSON, CDISC’s Excel template and ars_check.csv is downloaded; an error does not stop it. export_ars() writes the same files as before.

  • A step of your own R: its rules in full, and the sample in that form (0.0.2.9206, pair B of the user-program design). The rules next to the GUI | R program switch opens the seven rules (the datasets registered, the ARD through the report, what each step leaves, code inside the definition stays there, no library(), no side effects, one report), and the ja guide’s chapter 11 “自分の R の手順” says the same; the code cards’ tips point to them. The sample study’s two figures of their own code are figures whose content step is R: F-14-2-2 reads T-14-2-2’s ARD as ard (its ARD source) instead of the ARD file, and neither attaches packages – the review has nothing to say of them. A figure whose code reads an ARD records the definition it was made from and is to be made again when that ARD changes, as a designed one. The articles (ja guide, ja figures) and the README say three kinds of report, each step on screen or in R.

  • A figure’s size is set on its page (step 3), and the first page shows it (0.0.2.9206, tflspec >= 0.0.24.9102; the user’s request on F-14-2-1: the result pane showed no plot, and its size was in step 2). Step 3 of a figure has Figure size, the report sheet’s figure_width_in / figure_height_in (the user’s decisions): blank is the figure’s own size, as rtfreporter places an image – a design’s, the company’s figure style for its kind (figure_settings width / height), one of your own code’s 6.5 x 4.5 in – shown in the field; a number is that many inches; fit (the button Fit to the page) is the page’s body (its width; its height less the titles and footnotes); Its own size blanks both again. The figure is drawn at that size – its text the size its theme says – and placed so (fig_sized(), written once in programs/tfl/fig_setup.R; rtf_figures() gets a size only when it is not the figure’s own). Step 2 keeps only its dpi (company 300): the resolution, pixels = inches x dpi, never the size on the page. A step’s code editor fits a laptop’s screen with its header and check (and is dragged taller). The first page (sample) draws the figure in its body, as wide as on the page: a design’s, or one of your own code’s last run. The designer’s preview is drawn at the same size. A design’s old width, height and units (which never reached the RTF: a figure was drawn at 6.5 x 4.5 in) go.

  • A report is a table, a listing or a figure; its data step and its content step may each be your own R (0.0.2.9206, tflspec >= 0.0.24.9102; the user’s direction on 9191: “user code” was a fourth type forced into line; the design user-program-per-step-design-2026-10-12, D1-D7 as recommended). At the top of step 1 and step 2, GUI | R program: R program makes the whole step your code (the report sheet’s data_code / content_code, tflspec), instead of the definition; a step whose code is not blank is that code, and [GUI] again asks before the code goes. The data step leaves data (a figure: df), the content step content; the datasets it reads are registered above its code (the report’s datasets: the program reads them first, by their names in lower case), and its ARD is ard when the report reads one (a table’s own analyses or one taken in; a figure’s as its ARD source says). The code is checked as you write it (tflspec::tfl_check_code(): rules U01-U05 in the review too – a dataset it reads that is not registered, nothing left for the next step, files read or packages attached by the code itself, ard where the report reads none), and [Run the code] runs the program up to its report out of the app, naming the step and the line of an error. Code inside the definition stays where it was (a table’s rework, a listing’s – its process code now –, a figure’s code step). Existing studies are moved on opening, nothing lost: a report of type user becomes the type its ID says (F... a figure, L... a listing, else a table) with its code its content step’s, its datasets (and those its code names) the report’s and its ARD switch its ARD source; a table’s data code becomes its data step’s code; a figure written by hand, its content step’s (plot given as content, as its program did). The workbooks are read from a copy and written as they now are on the next save. step_code(), set_step_code(), report_datasets(), set_report_datasets(), preview_code() (was preview_user()); make_user_report() and the offer to convert figures written by hand are gone; add_output() has no data_code.

  • A figure’s data steps on any object (the user’s questions Q1-Q3 on 0.0.2.9186; tflspec >= 0.0.24.9102). A data step’s form has In and Out on one line at its foot: the object it reads and the one it leaves, each shown as it is when left empty (df, the object above, the step’s own name). Typed, a step works on another object (In: df, Out: df_ev makes df_ev and keeps df), a named step reads it (In: df_ev), or reads a dataset by its name (adsl). A second read makes df2 (was df again). The objects offered are those made before the step (tflspec::tfl_fig_objects()).

  • Two data steps: Any function (survival::survfit, ggsurvfit::survfit2 … suggested, any pkg::fn typed; its arguments in R, their names listed under the field; the object it reads given as its data) and ARD analysis (an ard_*() function of the catalog on an analysis data of the ARD definition): the step is the figure’s row of the ARD definition (its ID, function, data, arguments; the row’s other columns kept), made by its ARD program. A figure with no ARD then reads its own; one that reads a table’s keeps it (the step says its analysis is used once the figure reads its own). An analysis data of another report chosen is copied into the figure. The specific steps (Kaplan-Meier fit, summary statistics, rate, counts) stay. The ARD analysis step’s code box shows its row (KM: fn(data, args)), and its note on a figure reading a table’s ARD has a button to read its own.

  • A user-code report makes a table or a figure, as its ID says (the user’s report on F-14-2-1): F... a figure, else a table. A user-code figure’s steps are a figure’s (“1 Data”, “2 Figure”); the report list says “User code (Figure)”; a TOC’s type is compared with what it makes (a TOC’s Figure on a user-code figure is no change). (Until the report types become table, listing and figure, each step’s code its own.)

  • A figure that cannot be drawn says why, and the app’s log keeps it (the user’s F-14-2-3 / F-14-2-4 on a sample whose official run had stopped when the app closed). A figure whose ARD has no rows yet says which ARD and how to make it (step 1, or an official run); every drawing error goes to the app’s log. [Close] says when a run is going on: it stops with the app, its ARD and reports left unfinished.

  • The figure designer’s forms, for the expert (the standard-screen principle): a piece’s lead text is in its heading’s (i), a field’s help is its placeholder and tooltip (no line under it), and a named step’s name is its Out, beside In.

  • The treatment colours (tflspec #233, with tflspec 0.0.24.9098): the figures’ first arm is Okabe-Ito blue #0072B2 (was "blue"), so the sample’s KM and forest figures change colour slightly; more arms than the standard’s colours repeat them with a warning, and the figure check names the arms that share one. The company standards’ README says that the order of the treatment rows of figure_colors is the arms’ colour order (reorder the rows in the workbook to reorder the colours), and describes the optional treatment_shapes / treatment_linetypes of figure_settings (blank: not used), which give the arms point shapes and line types for print in black and white.

  • The generated programs, reviewed again (#347, with tflspec 0.0.24.9097). The sample’s tables and listing are the same RTF byte for byte; the two designed figures change on purpose:

    • A figure printing a table’s numbers shares its code lists (ard_source table:<id>): the KM figure F-14-2-3 shows Placebo, Low Dose, High Dose in the table’s order and colours (it was alphabetical, High Dose second). The forest plot F-14-2-4 has code lists of its own: its subgroups print as Female / Male, 18-64 years, and its subgroup axis has no title.
    • A failed program says why in the run’s record: R’s error output is kept beside the log (<program>.err) and, when logrx logged no error, its last Error line is the note of run.csv and of ard_status.csv (a package too old stopped a program with an empty note). broom (>= 1.0.8) and broom.helpers (>= 1.17.0) are required (what cardx’s models need), and the sample’s check says a version too old.
    • A report’s program names itself report_id: the study ARD’s rows, the program’s own path and the RTF’s (file.path(path_tfl, paste0(report_id, ".rtf"))); a program copied for another report changes one line.
    • Every program, ARD programs too, starts with a short check that it runs from the study folder (under 80 columns; a check in the setup could not run before the setup’s own source() fails); the banner’s description is wrapped; record_report()’s setup fingerprint is on lines of its own; a program ends on its last line.
    • The figure designer names the figure’s data as the program does (adtte_ttde, from tflspec::tfl_fig_data_name()) in step 1’s objects and the layers’ object choices, and a piece’s own lines of an ard_number layer are its label (ard_label_<k>) and its annotate(), not the later labels renumbered.
    • The sample: its stacked analysis is DEMOG (ard_demog, not a name of a cards function), its survival code writes the event CNSR == 0 and names the Cox model.

  • A study opens faster (#367; the user’s report: tens of seconds to minutes after opening a study or taking in a TOC). The report list and the review did the same work again for every report: the analysis data sheet is normalized once while it is the same, and whether a figure reads an ARD comes from its design (tflspec’s tfl_fig_uses_ard(), >= 0.0.24.9096) instead of writing its program. The review’s check of the programs (P02) asks the files’ times once, as numbers. With tflspec 0.0.24.9096’s faster figure checks and ARD fingerprints, on a study of 170 reports (a fresh R): the reports’ run state 2.3 -> 0.4 s, the report list 2.6 -> 0.7 s, the review 8.9 -> 7.2 s the first time and 4.2 s again; the app is idle about 20 s sooner after opening. The study ARD (output/ard/ard.rds) is read once while it is the same file (its time and size): every report’s rows, the figures’ and the conditions read it, once each. The same results (compared row for row).

  • The home is never inside the study folders (#359, the user’s requirement): tidying the studies would delete it. The home holds the study folders (<home>/studies, a new home’s default) or sits beside them (C:/tflplanner_home and C:/studies). setup_tflplanner(), the setup wizard and the app’s settings refuse a home inside the folder new studies go to, equal to it, or inside a study’s folder (the app says the place is not saved, and why). A home already there (set by an earlier version) is said on the Study tab, with how to move it in its (i); nothing is moved. The same for a new study’s place: create_study(), create_sample_study() and the new-study dialog (empty, a copy, the sample) refuse a place the home is in, or one inside a study’s folder – the dialog says so under the field, as for the ID – and register_study() a study folder the home is in.

  • A study folder at a drive’s root: C:/ and an ID give C:/ABC-101 (was C://ABC-101, which could not be written). A folder that cannot be made says which and why (“Could not make the folder … (reason)”, in the app’s language), not R’s “cannot open the connection”.

  • A study’s saved state is at <home>/state/<STUDY_ID> (was <home>/studies/<STUDY_ID>, now a new home’s study folders). An old one is moved on first use – moved, never deleted; an item already at the new place stays where it was. (Before, with the study folders at <home>/studies, a study’s folder was its state’s folder too, and unregistering the study removed it.)

  • A TOC taken in again: a report’s label, title or analysis set it prints all the same is no change. A report with no value of its own prints the study’s default ({OUTPUT_LABEL} “Table 14.1.1” from its id): a TOC saying the same was counted as a change (“add”) for every report of the sample. It is compared with what the report prints now. A report of one’s own code that the TOC calls a figure, or a type the TOC only guessed, is no change either (the type was never changed; every import again said two reports of the sample changed).

  • Two example TOCs made from the sample study, in system.file("extdata", package = "tflplanner"): SAMPLE-01_TOC.xlsx (its 17 reports with titles, analysis sets, sections, a Topline column and a shell sheet each) and SAMPLE-01_TOC_changed.xlsx (two rows changed), to try the import on the sample study: the first gives its reports their sections (and the Topline batch) and, taken in again, changes nothing; the second, taken in after it, shows two reports changed (a title, a footnote). data-raw/make-toc-sample.R makes them.

  • A study copied takes how it reads its TOC (input/toc/profile.yml: the rule set, the way the IDs are made, the sheets): the next study of the same company layout reads its TOC the same way. Not the TOCs taken in nor what they said: the copy’s TOC is its own. toc_copy_profile().

  • Step 3: one card, “Report information and tokens” (the user’s direction; first in the page form). The report list can only rename a report or take in a TOC, so the TOC’s information about a report is edited here: its label, title, analysis set text ({OUTPUT_LABEL}, {OUTPUT_TITLE}, {OUTPUT_POPULATION} – the report’s rows of the tokens sheet) and section ({OUTPUT_SECTION}, the report list’s section). Each field shows what a blank gives in its placeholder (the label made from the ID, step 1’s analysis set), and nothing under it: where a value came from is what a TOC taken in again lists (below), and the page’s sample shows what it prints; no reset button. The ID is read only, with a link to the report list. Below: the report’s own tokens (add, change, remove; a name of the report’s information or of rtfreporter’s is refused) and, folded, every token of rtfreporter’s with what it is, as rtfreporter::rtf_text_tokens() lists them ({AUTO_PAGE}, {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}, {BOOK_PAGE}, {PROGRAM_NAME} …). The Titles card says the title its header prints and where it changes; the titles’ and footnotes’ tokens are inserted from one list. The report picker of “Make a report” follows the title and section at once (the title of the report’s information first).

  • A TOC taken in again: what was edited here, kept or overwritten as chosen. A line or a report’s information (label, title, analysis set text, section) as the last TOC said follows the new TOC. One edited, or cleared, here is listed in “What would change” with the TOC’s text and “Use the TOC’s text” – unticked by default, so it stays – and one box takes the TOC’s text for everything edited here. (Before, a line edited here and not changed in the TOC was kept with no choice, and the information was not listed.) The section is one value, the report list’s (the TOC no longer writes an OUTPUT_SECTION row of the tokens sheet).

  • Two official runs compared (the Runs tab’s “Compare…”; compare_batches()). A run chosen in the runs table (else the newest) against the run of the same kind before it, or any two: the inputs that changed – the data by the md5 data_manifest.csv records, the code by the md5 of the kept code/; “not kept” when a run did not keep them – and the results that changed (identical, the same but the date and time a report prints, the same object, different, not made, new), said in two lines (“Inputs changed: … / Results changed: 2 of 30: …”) over a table of what changed, with a CSV. After a fix to the data or the programs, it shows that only what was fixed changed. The kept code now has programs/study_helpers.R (the study setup sources it), and a run keeps the reports’ status (output/tfl/report_status.csv) as it keeps the ARD’s.

  • An official run can keep its data (the Runs tab’s “keep the data in the batch folder”, off by default; run_batch(data = TRUE), the autoexec programs’ --data). The data files the run’s programs read – by the data catalog: each table’s datasets (an analysis data’s, those it is made from), a listing’s, a figure’s, an ARD taken in – are copied into the batch folder’s data/ under their path in the study folder, and listed with their size, md5 and time in data_manifest.csv. Ticked, the tab says how many files and how large before the run, and warns above 500 MB (options(tflplanner.batch_data_warn_mb)); batch_data_plan() gives the same list. Every official run now also writes session_info.txt – the packages its programs name with their versions, and sessionInfo() – and keeps the study’s renv.lock when it has one; batch.txt says whether the code and the data were kept, and the runs table has a Data column. With the code, the logs and the versions, a batch folder is everything the run read: the first step of the official-run snapshot (a run made again as it was, though the data change after). Save the study once so programs/batch.R knows the data.

  • The runs table says how each official run went (its State column, in place of Programs and Errors): running and for how long, done (when; every program without error), its errors, or not finished (stopped). The end of a run says the same in its message, with the time it took. A folder icon on each row opens the batch folder in Explorer, Finder or the file manager; it and “Open the batch folder” are shown only when the app runs on this computer. list_batches() has state and finished.

  • The days in a week, a month and a year come from the company standards (the user’s request). A figure’s time unit divides by named constants – days_per_week, days_per_month, days_per_year – not by numbers in each program (tflspec >= 0.0.24.9090 writes mutate(AVAL = AVAL / days_per_month)). The built-in standards’ setup_code sets them (7, 30.4375, 365.25), so a new study’s programs/study_setup.R part 1 has them, and a company changes them there. A study made before has none: the figure setup defines each with tflspec’s value when the study’s setup does not. The Plot Designer’s preview divides by the study’s own values (read from its setup file). No data column may share a constant’s name – the naming rule of the programs – and the review says so: rule D03, an error naming the dataset and the column, with the hint to rename it.

  • A run in the background never veils the page (the user’s report on this version). While its ARD programs ran, the page went white for an instant every few seconds with the busy cursor: the poll’s work (the marks worked out again) made the server busy, and the page’s veil – meant for the user’s own waits (opening a study, saving) – came up. The veil now comes only for a busy state that begins right after a click, a key or a changed field; the poll’s updates go by unseen.

  • Step 3’s form, the user’s notes (page patterns, 0.0.2.9187): a line a report of a pattern inherits from Standard says “Standard (= Compact)”; the font is Courier or Courier New to choose, or any typed (the defaults are rtfreporter’s: Letter, landscape, Courier 9 pt, 0.75 in margins); the titles’ heading says what it is – “The header’s {OUTPUT_TITLE}”, the text the header prints there, not a title line; the tokens card is above the header, with a token added (its name and text) or removed, and beside it what a header, footer, title or footnote can say, and where each comes from (made from the report’s ID, the TOC taken in, the study’s tokens, rtfreporter’s). The first page’s sample is fitted to the pane’s width by default. The pattern’s select and its button on one line, the same height.

  • {OUTPUT_POPULATION} by default the label of the report’s analysis set (step 1’s population), for a report no row of the tokens sheet says one for; a TOC taken in, or a value typed in step 3, is such a row and wins. It is not written to the sheets: the programs, the page’s sample and step 3’s list of tokens (which says where it comes from) see it. The same for tables, listings and figures.

  • The report list’s tokens are not set in the page form (the user’s rule). {OUTPUT_ID}, {OUTPUT_LABEL}, {OUTPUT_TITLE}, {OUTPUT_POPULATION} and {OUTPUT_SECTION} are listed read only under step 3’s tokens, each with where it comes from and a link to where it changes: the ID and label in the report list (Rename), the analysis set in step 1, the section in the report’s section (Data code). The title has one place: the Titles card’s “The header’s {OUTPUT_TITLE}” (a TOC taken in writes it), and the report list’s Title column now shows it first. The tokens card’s own rows are the page’s own tokens only; a token of a report list’s or rtfreporter’s name ({PAGE} …) is refused with a message. {OUTPUT_SECTION} is by default the report’s section, as {OUTPUT_POPULATION} its analysis set’s label.

  • The built-in standards name the analysis sets in full, by ICH E9’s names: Safety Analysis Set, Full Analysis Set, Per Protocol Set, Enrolled Set, Randomized Set, Pharmacokinetic Analysis Set (was “Safety set” and the like), so a report’s {OUTPUT_POPULATION} reads well by default. A study’s own populations sheet keeps its own labels.

  • The sample’s Compact keeps Standard’s paper (Letter): only the type (8 pt) and the margins (0.5 in) differ. The pattern dialog says that a pattern that changes the paper should say so in its name (A4_Compact).

  • The report marks follow a run report by report again (the user’s report on 0.0.2.9186). Since 0.0.2.9184 the marks of a run in the background changed only when the run had ended: a report’s mark needs its file, and the files were not watched. The reports’ output folder is watched now too (each report program writes its file once, so no churn): each mark turns as its report is made, still in place, the page never greyed.

  • A time-unit step in days says why it writes no line (the user’s report): the time is in days already (ADTTE’s AVAL), so step 1’s “Code of this piece” said “(nothing yet)”; it says so now, and months, weeks or years write the division (mutate(AVAL = AVAL / 30.4375)). The notes of that pane are in the app’s language.

  • The page patterns edited in a dialog (the page-patterns design, part C). “Edit the patterns…” on step 3 opens Standard and each pattern on the same form as a report’s page: a pattern’s values marked “this pattern” with “Back to Standard”, Standard’s own with “Clear”. New pattern (from Standard, no difference), Rename (the reports’ choice follows), Remove (refused while a report uses it, naming them); add_page_pattern(), rename_page_pattern(), remove_page_pattern(). The sample has one: Compact (A4, 8 pt, half-inch margins), used by T-14-3-1, the long AE table.

  • Titles and footnotes on step 3’s form (the page-patterns design, part B). The titles card has the heading – the report’s {OUTPUT_TITLE}, shown when its header prints one, as the sample’s and the company standards’ do – and the titles sheet’s lines; the footnotes card the footnotes’ lines. Each line as the header’s and footer’s: the report’s own to edit, its pattern’s or Standard’s to change here or leave out here. Insert buttons put a token – the report’s ({OUTPUT_LABEL}, {OUTPUT_TITLE}, {OUTPUT_POPULATION}), the study’s, rtfreporter’s ({PAGE}, {PROGRAM}, {DATETIME} …) – into the field last clicked, at the cursor.

  • Page patterns, and step 3 as a form (the page-patterns design, part A; _archive/tflplanner-page-patterns-design.md). A study keeps named page patterns besides Standard – rows of the report half’s sheets whose output_id is @ and a name (@Compact), saying only what differs from Standard (tflspec >= 0.0.24.9089 reads them) – and a report chooses one in step 3 (“Page pattern”; the new report$pattern column). Step 3 is a form now: the paper, margins and font, the header and footer lines and the tokens, each value with where it comes from – this report, its pattern, Standard – and “Back to the pattern” where the report has its own. A value the pattern already gives is no difference (no own cell is written); a line of the pattern’s can be changed here or left out here ((none)), or added for this report. The form writes only the report’s own rows; the sheets themselves are under “Details: edit the sheets” (the same rows). A pattern’s rows (@...) are not a report (output_ids()); an @ starts no report’s ID. Patterns are written in the sheets for now; editing them in a dialog, and titles / footnotes as a form, come next.

  • A TOC taken in by the company’s rules (#299, phases 1 and 2 of its plan). The company standards keep one rule set or several for TOCs: toc_map gains a rule_set column (blank: standard) and the new sheet toc_rules holds a set’s settings – TOC and Topline sheet names, header rows, phase values and suffixes, the Topline flag’s values and batch, the phase-specific shell sheet names, how the output id is made. A workbook written before reads as one set, standard, as today. The built-in draft has standard and two-phase.

    • Found, not chosen: each file is read once; its TOC sheet is the one named as the set names it, else the one whose rows match the most column names (more rows on a tie); the header row is found in the first rows (a heading above it is fine). A second TOC-like sheet (a Topline sheet) is a cross-check, never the source. A cover sheet, a shells-only workbook and a document that is no table are said.
    • The rule set picked on the TOC’s column names (the most items matched), shown with its score and changeable.
    • The output id built by a rule chosen per set (the maintainer’s decision on D3): an id column as it is, normalised ({type}.{number}, {TYPE}-{number-}: prefix t./f./l. added or removed, . and -), a type column and a number column, or the number in the first title (“Table 14.1.1”). The one that gives unique ids for the most rows is proposed with a preview of its ids, and can be changed; “remember” keeps the choice in the set. The type comes from a type column, the id’s prefix or the first title’s first word; the label (“Table 14.1.1”) from a label column or the first title.
    • One report a phase: a both row gives two reports, the phase’s suffix on the id and label (.a / .b) and on a title line (” - Phase 1 Part”); a study’s own suffixes are kept in its profile.
    • Shell sheets linked across every file (a phase’s -1 / -2 first), only the link: input/toc/shells.csv (toc_shell_links()).
    • The Topline batch from the flag column into the report list’s batches column; the Topline sheet is compared with it (warnings).
    • The problems table (#288’s shape, area = "toc", rules TOC01-TOC12): errors stop “Take it in”, rows not read are listed to set by hand, the rest are warnings. Kept as input/toc/problems.csv.
    • The record (input/toc/imports.csv) gains rule_set, standards_md5, sources, unread, warnings; every file is copied; the study’s choices go to input/toc/profile.yml and pre-fill the next import.
    • The dialog (Take in a TOC…) takes several files, shows each one’s sheet and header row with the reason, the rule set, how the ids are made, the phase suffixes, a preview of the reports (phase, label, titles, shell, batch), the rows not read and the warnings; the analysis sets, datasets and “what would change” are as before.
    • In R: toc_rules(), toc_source(), toc_find_sheet(), toc_find_header(), toc_pick_rules(), toc_map_for(rule_set =), toc_id_candidates(), toc_rows(), toc_expand_phases(), toc_link_shells(), toc_batches(), toc_import_read(), toc_import_spec(), toc_problems(), toc_apply_extras(), toc_profile(), toc_shell_links(). With tflspec’s tfl_read_toc() on a data frame (tflspec #217) the reports are read without a temporary file; with an older tflspec a temporary .csv is used.

  • A figure’s steps: “1 Data” and “2 Figure” (#293, the user’s figure feedback; design note _archive/fig-step1-design-2026-10-11.md). A figure’s step 1 is mostly preparing its data, an ARD only sometimes: it is named “1 Data” (a table’s stays “1 ARD”) and holds the figure’s data steps – their list and form, moved from the designer – with “Numbers from an ARD (optional)” below them. Step 2, “2 Figure”, keeps the figure settings and the layers, laid out as a table’s step 2: the pieces and the form at the left, the figure at the right (Design | Edit | Preview). Step 1 also shows what the steps make – df, a KM fit, the ARD’s statistics – each in short (its size, columns, first rows; or the first lines it prints), made on demand (“Preview the data”) or kept from the last drawing; preview_figure() returns them as objects.

  • One rule for the names tflplanner gives an analysis data: <dataset>_<population>[_<PARAMCD>] – adsl_saf, adae_saf, adtte_saf_ttde (was adtte_ttde: the parameter alone, in one name, the population in the next). Only a condition’s parameter is in the name; a visit or another condition is the label’s. Only the defaults: a name given stays. The sample follows it: adtte_ttde is adtte_saf_ttde, advs_w24 is advs_saf_sysbp (its programs change by the names only). Needs tflspec >= 0.0.24.9087 (the forest template’s data named so).

  • A run in the background no longer greys the page (the user’s report on 0.0.2.9175). Following a run the app did not start made the whole page be drawn again every few seconds (each ARD program, each preview log), greyed and not taking clicks for a moment. Now only what changed follows it: the report list’s marks are changed in place (the list is not drawn again), the ARD’s state is worked out again only when the report chosen has its ARD made, and every report’s once when the run has ended; the Runs tab’s tables when a batch ends. The logs are not watched any more. Checked on R 4.6.1: the sample’s official run, 160 s, sitting on Make a report and on the report list – nothing faded, the marks from “not made” to “made” without a reload. (Steps 2 and 3’s marks, never drawn, no longer stay “recalculating” either.)

  • The forest plot from the figure’s own ARD (#293 phase 6, with tflspec’s forest_hr in parts). The hazard ratios, intervals and N a forest plot prints are statistics of the figure’s own ARD – a Cox model of all subjects and one within each subgroup variable, by cards / cardx – not fitted inside the figure program. set_fig_own_analyses() writes the analyses a design brings (attr(design, "analyses")) to the figure’s ARD definition and sets its source to own; the Plot Designer’s forest template does so when applied, with the subgroups and the arm compared chosen on its form. The sample gains F-14-2-4, the hazard ratio of the time to first dermatologic event by sex and age group. Needs tflspec >= 0.0.24.9084.

  • Ready for CRAN’s checks, the parts that do not wait for the submission (#334). The tests that start the app or write study folders (5-10 s a test: the spec workbooks) skip on CRAN – 16 files, skipped as a whole, and every app-server block – and still run on CI and locally (NOT_CRAN=true): CRAN’s test run, measured as CRAN runs it, takes 5 minutes on a Windows laptop instead of 16 (the pure-function tests stay: planner, standards, spec import, figure design, …), and its one warning (the ARS reader’s, on the sample) is gone; app_server()’s three local one() helpers have names of their own (one_val, toc_row, header_line: no “multiple local function definitions” NOTE); the examples of setup_tflplanner(), create_study(), reload_from_spec() and create_sample_study() run, with a home in the temporary folder (the study-writing ones in \donttest{}, a few seconds each), and add_shortcut() / update_tflplanner() say why theirs are not run. The title is “‘shiny’ Study Manager for Clinical Tables, Listings and Figures”; the language en-GB, as rtfreporter’s and tflspec’s; the word list has the CDISC names and the rest spelling flags; inst/COPYRIGHTS links the licence instead of the build-ignored LICENSE.md; the package help says where to start.

  • The sample’s race tables are demographics tables, with ASIANSUB (the user’s request on #326). T-14-1-5 and T-14-1-6 show age (n, mean (SD), median, min and max), age group, sex and ethnicity as well, so RACE is the one variable with rows nested under one of its levels. The derived sub-category is ASIANSUB, one column per race as an EDC collects it (White’s would be WHTSUB, nested under “White”: each its own analysis, plan_nest() takes several), still footnoted as derived for demonstration. The other reports’ programs and RTFs are byte-identical.

  • The app follows a run that ends, without a reload (#305 area). After a background official run (the sample’s, for one), the report list kept every report “not made” and a table’s builder said “no ARD yet” until the browser was reloaded. The app now watches what a run writes in the study folder – the study ARD’s status, a batch’s run.csv, a preview’s log – every few seconds, and refreshes the marks and the ARD state when they change, whoever ran it (this session, another, the app before a restart, R); and the builder reads a table’s ARD for itself again then.

  • A report’s Total column switched itself on after a reconnect (#331 follow-up). The table builder’s inputs are numbered by the form drawn (b3_total_on), from 0 in each session; a browser reconnecting to a new session (the app restarted) sends the inputs it still holds, and an earlier form’s switch, on, was read as this form’s: the Total column turned on for a report without one, unsaved, and its preview stopped in plan_total(). The numbering now starts at a random point in each session, so no input of a session before is read as one of this session’s form – for every builder field, not only the switch.

  • An ARD definition that does not hold is said, not passed over (#323). Saving writes no ARD program then (a blank from of an analysis data made by code, for one); it used to say nothing, and the official run failed on every ARD program with “cannot open the connection”. Now save_study() says so in a message and keeps it as $ard_problem (the app shows it after Save, the rest still saved), the Review tab’s error row says that no ARD program is written, the runner says “no program …: save the study” for a program that is not there instead of running it, and run_batch() on a study with no ARD programs names the likely cause.

  • A Total column, without a “Total” arm in the data (tflspec #212, rtfreporter plan_total()). set_total_column(x, output_id, label, position) switches it on in both halves of a table’s definition: the tables sheet’s total / total_position (written as plan_total()), and overall = TRUE on the report’s own analyses grouped by the column variable (not the rows inside a stack, not custom / subjects), which makes each ARD program run them again without their by – cards’ own overall rows, with no group. The ARS then has an analysis over all subjects without the grouping, not a "Total" group the ADaM does not have. Needs tflspec >= 0.0.24.9083 and rtfreporter >= 0.8.2.9034.

  • Logistic and Poisson regressions on R before 4.4 need MASS (#319). Before R 4.4, confint() of a glm comes from MASS, and without it cardx::ard_regression() stops with “Unable to tidy x”. MASS is installed with R, so this concerns only an R where it was removed: the ARD dictionary’s help for these two models says so, and its test skips them only where MASS cannot be loaded.

  • Step 3 (page and output): the input on the left again, the page at its actual size (the user’s request). The report’s page sheets (report, page, header, footer, titles, footnotes, your tokens) are the form on the left, as before the SPEC | Code | Result tabs came (that change had put them inside the SPEC tab); on the right the tabs open on Result: the first page at 100%, scrolling in its pane, with a “Fit to width” button (remembered in the browser) and “Full size” as before. SPEC shows the report’s own rows as they are written to spec/report_spec.xlsx, read only. The report’s font stays above. ## Upgrading from an earlier version

Update tflplanner and tflspec together, open each study and save it, then look at its Review tab.

  • This tflplanner needs tflspec 0.0.24.9079 or later (0.0.2.9157 and later needed 0.0.24.9077): update both together.
  • Six functions are no longer tflspec’s; the study keeps them in programs/study_helpers.R. set_levels(), tag_ard(), fmt_ard(), keep_stats(), fmt_pvalue() and save_ard() (tflspec’s up to 0.0.24.9066) are written there by a save, and the study’s setup sources it. A program that calls them as tflspec:: or after library(tflspec) without it stops; the review says which (P02): write it again (open the study and save) or source programs/study_helpers.R.
  • A figure design written before reads as it is: its YAML’s old form (stats:, data_code, stats_code) is read, and a save writes the new one.
  • Figure programs have a new shape, and draw the same figures: a data and a plot section, one + chain. A save writes them again.
  • The steps: update both packages; open each study and save it (the programs and study_helpers.R are written again; a program edited by hand is copied to programs/.edited/ first); check the Review tab.

Changes

  • The table builder says what the report’s ARD holds. Above the SPEC / Code / Result tabs, one line: the column variables and their groups, the pages, the rows, the analysis variables (categorical, continuous), the statistics and when the ARD was read (“ARD: columns TRT01A (3 groups) | 6 variables …”); opened, a small table of each one’s role, kind, levels or statistics and label. “Show the whole normalized ARD” opens it in a dialog – paged, filterable, the main columns or all – read only then. From what reading the ARD saved: nothing more is read to draw the card.

  • Race with its Asian sub-categories, nested or in two blocks (the sample’s T-14-1-5 and T-14-1-6, with rtfreporter #599 and tflspec #213). The table builder’s variable form gets “Rows under a level of another variable”: a categorical variable’s rows go right after the chosen level’s row of another, one step deeper, without their own heading (the variables sheet’s under, written as plan_nest()). The sample gains the two tables from the same data and analyses:

    • T-14-1-5: Race, n (%) with Chinese / Japanese / Korean under Asian.
    • T-14-1-6: Race, n (%), then Race Sub Asian.

    They count the enrolled subjects (a new analysis set ENR, all of ADSL: the pilot’s two Asian subjects are screen failures) by ARM, with a Total column. The Asian sub-categories are derived for demonstration (a footnote says so; RACE is not changed). The other tables’ programs and RTFs are byte-identical.

  • The Review tab says in plain words what reading the data does. The internal “data facts” are gone from the screen and the guide: the button is “Review with the data” (データも使って見直す) everywhere, and the tab says “The checks against the data have not run yet. Press [Review with the data] to read the datasets once (not again until a file changes).”

  • The preview shows a column header line’s bold and underline. Ticked in the table builder (a line’s “bold”, “underline”), they were in the definition, the program and the RTF, but the Result tab’s preview drew every header cell plain. It now draws a header cell bold, with its rule above or below and its alignment, as the RTF prints it.

  • A figure printing a table’s numbers is in the ARS export (#293 phase 5, with tflspec #211). export_ars() passes the figures whose ARD is a table’s, with the analyses their designs print, to tflspec::tfl_ars(references =): the sample’s F-14-2-3 is an ARS Output (its titles and RTF) whose list of contents names T-14-2-2’s KM and HR analyses, no longer “no analyses in the ARD definition”.

  • A figure printing a table’s numbers follows that table’s ARD (#293 phase 4). Its program records the definition of the ARD it read (ard_built <- ard_fingerprint("T-14-2-2"), then record_report(report_id, ard = ard_built): a column ard in output/tfl/report_status.csv). study_status() marks it outdated when the table’s ARD is not made from the table’s definition now, or when it was made from another definition than the figure; its new column why says why a report is to be made again (program, setup, ard:<id>), shown in the runs table. The official run of the reports (programs/batch.R: .batch_needs, .batch_needs_hash) and the preview (run_study()) make the table’s ARD first when it is not made from its definition – logged in the same batch under ard – and leave it alone when it is. After this update every report program is rewritten once (record_report() changed in report_setup.R).

  • The column header form, easier to read and to use (step 2, the table builder). Each line’s tools (its number, its shape, alignment, bold, underline, the arrows) are on top of its fields, on a grey band with a rule above, so where one line ends and the next starts is plain; the insert chips and “what the header’s {n} counts” are in boxes of their own. “From a preset…” is a button the size of the others, “Load a standard column header…”, next to “Add a line above”; it opens a list of the standard headers, each with its lines in short.

  • What the header’s {n} counts, chosen among the ARD’s numbers. The choices are the populations the ARD states for the table’s columns (rtfreporter’s plan_n_candidates()), each with its values: one (“Subjects, by TRT01A: 86 / 84 / 84”, chosen); on pages split by a lab parameter two, “Subjects on each page (per PARAMCD, by TRT01A): 22 / 24 / 23” and “Analysis set (by TRT01A, the same on every page): 25 / 26 / 24”, and both. When the two differ and none is chosen the form says so (making the report warns until then); with no ARD yet the three in words. The choice is the tables sheet’s header_n, as before. Needs rtfreporter 0.8.2.9033.

  • The table builder says only what fits the table (#324). The note “Check this order: the data do not give one …” under a column variable’s order no longer shows when the report has a code list for that variable (its ARD program puts the columns in the list’s order); the form says the order is the code list’s instead. A table with no continuous variable no longer shows the continuous rows, “A row of your own” and the decimals of their statistics, nor warns that the ARD has no mean, sd …; what the definition says of them is kept as it is.

  • A new report goes where its id sorts; the list can be sorted by ID. The report list’s order is still the order the reports are made in. A report added (Add, Copy, add_output(), copy_output()) goes where its id sorts among the others – by the numbers in the id, as numbers (T-14-1-2 after T-14-1-1 and before T-14-1-10; T-14-0-1 before F-14-2-1, the sections’ order), then its letters – instead of last; one ordered by hand keeps its order. A TOC’s reports come in the TOC’s order (add_output(at = "end")). The report list’s new “Sort by ID” puts the whole list in that order, after asking how many move; the up and down arrows still move one. sort_outputs() does the same in R.

  • The review names a program calling a function tflspec no longer has (P02, area program): one of the six above, as tflspec::, or after library(tflspec) with programs/study_helpers.R not sourced on the way (an error; to check when another program sources it). The study’s programs/ is looked at, not its copies in .edited/.

  • The review lists a figure’s ARD problems (#288). A figure that prints a table’s numbers is reviewed as the catalog’s F04-F08: its ARD source is not a table of the study (F04), the design reads an ARD but the figure has none (F05), a piece names an analysis the table no longer has (F06), the ARD is not made yet (F07), a piece the ARD cannot answer (F08). A click on one opens the figure’s step 2, or the piece in the designer.

  • The review’s sentences in Japanese, values and all. A row carries its sentence (template) and values (args); the app translates the sentence and puts the values in. With tflspec 0.0.24.9078 that covers a table against its ARD (T06, T07), a listing’s columns (L01, L02) and a figure against the data (F03); the app’s own figure rules (F04-F07) too.

  • The Review tab (#288, phase 2). A tab between Make a report and Runs lists the study’s review (study_review()): what cannot be used, what is probably wrong, what to set by hand, report by report (the picker on the left, each report with its three counts), filtered by level, area and a search. A click on an item goes to it: the report chosen, its step and tab, the analysis, analysis data, code list or figure piece opened, and the grid’s row and cell flashed.

    • The review is the app’s one: made when a study is opened, 2 s after edits pause and after a save (no file read: the facts of the data kept from the last read); Review with the data reads the files whose facts are stale; Check as the programs read it is the former Runs tab’s definition check (its card is gone).
    • Its counts where one works: the report head (each a link to the tab, that report and level), the report picker (errors / to check / by hand after each title, the run’s mark as it was), and the analyses’ badges (an error, or something to check: the subjects per group counted twice among them) read the review instead of the ARD definition’s message.
    • A figure’s advice with a one-step fix has an Apply button.
    • The company standards’ settings key review_off (A12 | C02) leaves rules out of every study’s review; the tab says which.
    • study_review(progress = ) / review_facts(progress = ): told the dataset each time one is read.
    • The guide (Japanese) has a section on the review.

  • The sample’s F-14-2-3 prints the hazard ratios too (#311). T-14-2-2’s ARD has a Cox model’s hazard ratios against placebo (a custom analysis HR, cardx::ard_regression(coxph(), exponentiate = TRUE)), in the ARD and not in the table (its cells name prob and time only; its RTF is unchanged, byte for byte), and F-14-2-3 prints each with its CI on one line, through tflspec’s labels that name several statistics of one address (HR {estimate} (95% CI {conf.low}, {conf.high}), tflspec #206). cardx::ard_regression() needs broom.helpers: it is in Suggests, and the sample’s official run names it among what to install when it is missing.

  • A figure prints the numbers of a table’s ARD (#293 phase 3, with tflspec #203). A figure’s step 2 (ARD) chooses where its ARD comes from: none (it reads its data only), its own analyses (defined as a table’s), or a table’s ARD (ard_source = table:<id> on the report row; set_fig_ard_source()), shown with the table’s analyses, the statistics its ARD has and which the figure uses. The program reads it as ard at the top of # ---- data ----; the Plot Designer offers “A number from the ARD” (a median, a hazard ratio … printed on the plot) and “Statistics from the ARD” (a data frame of them) when the figure has one, with the analyses, variables and statistics of that ARD to choose from, and the preview draws them. The study’s check names a source that is not a table, a design that reads an ARD without one, an ARD not made yet (a warning), and a piece whose analysis, statistic, level or group the ARD does not have. Renaming a table renames its figures’ table: references. The sample’s F-14-2-3 prints the three medians of T-14-2-2’s ARD; the number at risk stays the fit’s.

  • A review of the whole study (#288, phase 1: the R functions; the Review tab comes next). study_review(study) lists, report by report, what cannot be used (error), what is valid but probably wrong (check) and what is missing and has to be set by hand (hand), each with where it is (sheet, the row’s key, column), a hint and its rule: tflspec’s rules (tflspec::tfl_review_rules()) on the study’s definition, and the report list’s and the study folder’s own – a report with no title (no title line, no OUTPUT_TITLE), no analysis set (a table whose analyses name none; its own code chooses itself), an analysis set the populations do not have, nothing that makes it (no analyses or data code, no listing columns, no figure design), an id twice or one a file name cannot hold, two reports writing one file or program, a dataset the list names that the catalog lacks (R01-R08); analyses of no report, an analysis reading another analysis set than its report’s, the subjects per group counted twice (A11-A13); a dataset with no file, for the study and under each report reading it (D01); and, with deep = TRUE, the definition read back as the programs read it (check_planner(), P01).

    • data = "read" checks against the data too: the facts of the data (review_facts(): each column’s class and values, each analysis set’s subjects, each condition’s rows – no records) are kept in the store, one file a dataset, and made again only for a dataset whose file (path, time, size) or definition (its analysis data, analyses, listings) changed. data = "cached" uses them and reads no file (a dataset not read yet says so, D02); "none", the definition alone.
    • ard = TRUE checks each table against what the study ARD holds and lists what went wrong while it was made (kept while ard.rds does not change).
    • The messages are in the app’s language, made from each rule’s template (one line a rule in strings.csv); message_en keeps the English. review_problems(x) reviews a definition with no study (an import’s draft).
    • On the sample study: no error and nothing to set by hand; 11 checks (9 code list values no record has, the KM figure’s two advices).

  • An edit makes the app work out only what depends on it; a save is quicker. Measured on the sample study (the profile of each action):

    • An edit of a table’s cell no longer hashes every report’s ARD definition again (the ARD’s state), rebuilds the report list, or reads the own ARD functions’ files: each now follows its part of the definition (the ARD definition and code lists; what the report list shows), not every change of it. The report list tab used the ARD’s state worked out a second time: it shares the one.
    • A save gave the study anew, and every output that asks whether a study is open – most – was drawn again (the table builder’s form among them, about a second): now only what the save changed is (the study list, the marks).
    • A save writes only the workbook whose half changed: a table’s cell edited, table_spec.xlsx alone (and the reports whose definition did not change no longer look outdated for the other). A program’s checksum is worked out once a program, in one file of the session’s (each was a new file, made and deleted, two or three times a program).
    • write_planner(books = ): "table", "report" or both (the default).

  • A designed figure’s program reads as one written by hand (#293, with tflspec #201). Its code has two sections, # ---- data ---- (the code lists, the datasets read, the steps’ pipes) and # ---- plot ---- (the palette, then one + chain into plot), before the report’s. The study’s fig_setup.R attaches the packages the figures use (ggplot2, patchwork, dplyr, and ggsurvfit for a KM), so a program has no library() of its own; it is sourced at the program’s top, beside the report setup, and the banner says the design is the place to edit. The number at risk is, by default, a plot of its own below the curves, its counts from the fit at the x axis’s breaks (summary(fit, times = ...)), joined with patchwork; its new “Drawn as” choice gives ggsurvfit’s add_risktable() instead. The Plot Designer’s data steps are one list: a KM fit, summary statistics … are steps that make an object of their own, and the steps after one go on in its pipe (the “Statistics” part is gone; a design saved before reads as one list). A step added goes after the one chosen, a step on df before the first object. “This piece’s code” shows the lines the script has with the piece and not without it.

  • A code list edited where it is used. The code lists’ part of 1-1’s column definitions (part 4), of a listing’s data and of a figure’s data lists each column with a list; a click opens that column’s values, labels and order in a grid right below, in place – one grid at a time (a click on another column moves it, on the same one closes it). A column without a list starts one from the select beside the buttons; “Add them to the list” opens the list it adds to; Copy… and the dialog of every code list (All code lists…, with reading a file) stay.

  • The table builder’s rows as the code list of variable. Under the variables in order, “As the code list of variable” opens a grid like the code lists’: each variable (value), the heading the table prints (label) and its place (order). It is the same thing as the list and its labels above, kept in one place – the variables sheet’s label and order – and the program still writes plan_labels(variable = c(...)): no new sheet or column.

  • The builder’s form, drawn again after an edit that changes its shape (a heading or the order above, a row of one’s own), keeps the page where it was instead of jumping to the top.

  • The launcher’s icon is the hex logo (#291). The desktop and Start menu shortcut (add_shortcut()) shows the package’s logo at 128 px and up; at the sizes the desktop and the taskbar use (24 to 64 px) a plain hexagon with a “t”, at 16 px the hexagon alone, so it stays clear. data-raw/launcher-icons.R makes the .ico, .png and .icns.

  • The report list shows and edits the named batches (#301): a Batches column, and Batches… for the report chosen – the names in use to choose from, a new one typed.

  • An official run of some of the reports (#301). The Runs tab lists the reports of a run, all ticked (All / None); a report unticked is left out – its ARD program and its report program – and a report the run makes that reads the ARD of one left out is said before the run. run_batch(exclude = ) does it in R (only = stays), the runner takes --exclude=<program>, and the batch folder’s batch.txt lists what was left out (the runs table too).

  • Named batches (#301; #299 D6): a set of reports an official run takes by name – Topline, Interim Analysis, Final. A report’s batches are the report list’s new batches column (| between several), so a later TOC import can fill it; batch_sets(), set_batch(), rename_batch(), remove_batch(). programs/batch.R carries them as .batch_sets; Rscript programs/autoexec_all.R --batch Topline and run_batch(batch = "Topline") run one, into runs/<date>_<time>_all_Topline/, its batch.txt naming it. In the Runs tab: choose a named batch (its reports ticked), save the ticks under a name (or over one), rename, delete. The full run is every report and has no name.

  • Edit the definition outside the app: export, edit the copy, import (#274, phase 2). Export the definition files (Study tab, Files) gives a zip of spec/ and study.yml, the ARD definition as an Excel workbook; Import definition files takes an edited copy back (workbooks known by their sheets, so a renamed copy works; .yml, .json or the zip). Before anything changes, the copy is checked in a temporary folder: every reader, every cell that holds R (conditions, derived columns, args, post, code, figure-design code) parsed, the ARD definition and figure designs checked, and the programs of the reports it touches written and parsed. Errors list file, sheet, row, column and problem and change nothing; warnings are shown and do not stop it. The parts that differ are listed to choose from; the study’s files are copied to spec/.backup/<date>-<time>/ first, then the study is saved. R: export_spec_files(), preview_spec_import(), import_spec_files(). A direct edit of spec/ is still found on open and goes through the same checks: a study whose files changed opens with a notice and “What changed”; files that do not read show a card (and a mark in the bar) with Load from the definition files and Write the files back from the last save, and the study cannot be saved until one is chosen; a save after an outside edit asks to load first; loading keeps unsaved changes and a draft, merged part by part (a part both changed asks which to keep). The Japanese guide’s 3.1 says how. The Japanese of tflspec’s texts that now say “population” (tflspec #197: the figure designer, figure advice, five column descriptions) follows them.

  • A new study from the sample is ready at once (#297). The sample is copied (seconds) and opened; its official run, which makes its ARD and reports (a few minutes), runs in the background as the Runs tab starts one. The study is in the list straight away, marked “(running)” until the run ends, and the app can be used meanwhile (before, it waited for the whole run with a progress note).

  • R-CMD-check now also runs on R 4.2, the oldest R tested (Depends: R (>= 4.1) is kept; cardx, used by the generated ARD code, needs R >= 4.2).

  • A study opens in a fifth of a second (#296, reported by the user). Reading a study from its saved state built every sheet’s columns with tflspec::tfl_table_spec() again, sheet by sheet, on every open and twice on every save; they are made once a session now. open_study(): 1.8 s to 0.15 s (the sample study); a save that changes nothing 5.6 s to 2.0 s; copying the sample (without its run) 9 s to 5

    1. The study list is drawn while the Study tab is hidden too, so a study made from another tab is in it when the tab is shown.

  • No links to discussions by number, and no code copied from one (#298): the tests that run the example workbooks of tflspec (>= 0.0.24.9071) follow their new contents.

  • The English screens say “population” (tflspec #191). “Analysis set” and “population” were mixed; the screens, messages and the company standards’ sheet description now say population (the Japanese stays 解析対象集団). The argument hints follow tflspec’s new wording, so their Japanese is found again. The Japanese guide says that a population is ICH E9 / CDISC ARS’s analysis set (analysisSetId in ARS). The SPEC, the ARD and the tokens (population_id, the populations sheet, {OUTPUT_POPULATION}) are as they were.

  • A report’s code lists are where its data is made: one place on the screen, one in the definition, one in the program. Step 1 (Code lists) is gone, and the steps are 1 ARD, 2 Content, 3 Page and output (1-1, 1-2 as they were 2-1, 2-2).
